content:
Maya: Heads up — after merging the AWQ conversion for gpt-j-6B (v2) we started seeing intermittent OOMs on our x1-dedicated pools. Memory graphs show a steady climb in the 'workspace' allocation and repeated small slab allocations around long sequences (seq_len ~2048). Repro attached below in case someone wants to run locally.

Sam: Noted. Do we know the KV cache dtype coming out of the converter? AWQ path has been defaulting some kv buffers to fp16/fp32 if we don't explicitly force int8, which would explain a ~2x jump.

Josh: I pulled a quick profile from one of the failed runs. Key bits: total_gpu_mem: 31.2GB, reserved_workspace: 4.1GB, kv_cache_bytes: 1.84GB. Expected kv_cache_bytes for this model on int8 path is ~920MB. Also the allocator exposes fragmentation_score rising from 0.12 -> 0.47 over ~3 minutes. Snippet: ```
# profiler summary
model: gpt-j-6B-awq-v2
seq: 2048
batch: 4
kv_cache_bytes: 1840123456
workspace_reserved: 4123456789
fragmentation_score: 0.47
common_alloc_paths: [alloc_slow_path, repeated_realloc]
```

Anya: Two quick things to try before rolling back: 1) force kv dtype to int8 with our runtime flag `REDWOOD_KV_DTYPE=int8` (this is a runtime cast + scale lookup we shipped last quarter), 2) cap workspace growth via `REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MAX=256M` to avoid runaway reservations while we diagnose. Also set `REDWOOD_ALLOC_HINT=compact` to bias the allocator to reuse freed blocks.

DevInfraBot: Deploy note: canary 2026-02-18T12:03:11Z applied AWQ conversion to 10% of traffic on x1 pool. Increase in OOM rate detected 12:10Z — alert routed to eng-runtime oncall.

Ryan: I reproduced locally with this quick harness: ```./stress_test --model gpt-j-6B --quant awq --seq 2048 --batch 4 --requests 1000``` OOMs consistently around request ~180-220 when default configs are used. I tried patching the runtime to cast kv cache to uint8+scale (cheap mem) and reusing the per-request temp buffer for prefix caching; result: no OOMs after 1000 requests and avg latency +3%.

Sam: If kv dtype is the main driver, we should also check the converter flags. AWQ conversion job may have flipped `keep_fp_kv=true` for stability; if so we should revert or add an explicit `--kv-dtype=int8` option to the pipeline and make runtime respect it.

Maya: Plan: (1) Ryan/Anya to run quick canary that sets `REDWOOD_KV_DTYPE=int8` + `REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MAX=256M` on canary nodes and report OOMs in 30m. (2) Josh to dig into allocator traces (alloc_slow_path) and see which kernel fallback is causing repeated reallocs. (3) If canary looks good we push hotfix to remaining nodes and add converter guard to production CI.

Josh: I'll pull the allocator traces and post a short flamegraph. Suspect the kernel-selection fallback from `fused_attention_fp8 -> generic_attention` is forcing temporary buffers to be allocated per-step. If so, we can add a fast-path kernel or pre-allocate a persistent temp buffer.

Maya: SG. I'll own rollout coordination. Assigning: Josh (allocator traces & kernel routing), Ryan (canary + repro harness), Anya (runtime flags + quick config patch). I'll post results in 45m. :thumbsup:

Ryan: Quick note — when you run the canary, include `--trace-alloc=short` so we capture the repeating alloc IDs; that helped me pinpoint the reclaim failure.

Maya: Thanks all — let's sync in thread. If anyone finds an urgent regression call it out with @eng-runtime oncall.
